[h3]Help! I've been Ass-Slapped with a Portuguese Man 'O' War! and ~30 other half-baked stories that probably aren't worth your time.[/h3]

Play experience: I got through maybe 3/4 of it, dropped it, read all of Umineko, contemplated buying more VNs, then started back from the beginning 5 years later to clear out the VNs I already own. I got through one ending: -Himeno-. Maybe I'll go back to try and figure out what was going on with Kenji eventually, but this game has bored me away from it.

Music was pretty good, visuals were overall great (I'm not the biggest fan of how non-chibi characters are drawn outside of maybe Kenji though that's obvs subjective, the backgrounds are absolutely gorgeous), translation was discernably B-A-D BAD, and the mediocre plot doesn't help.

I actively felt this game try to kill any interest I had in it every time Mayu opened her mouth. Not that Mayu is an unlikable character, on the contrary, I REALLY wanted to like her as a protagonist! But all of her growth (and she's really the only character that seems to GET "growth") is very tell-don't-show-or-do. She's very flimsy as a person, and so is Himeno. I just can't get over how unrealistic the both of them feel as middle school girls (I was one of those once, I should know). They have a conceptually sweet dynamic, but this game is OBSESSED with tell-don't-show. A lot of the game's problems lie in that you just can't feel a lot of the things that they want you to with characters as flat as this.

I can feel the narrative slowly try and destroy itself the further on I read. Despite my initial wonder at the gorgeous backdrops of the mysterious Manten Aquarium, what we have is a collection of setpieces and the little one-note goonies that run around it to TRY and make it work, through clunky-sounding exposition. And, considering my dwindling lack of interest as the game went on, it sadly failed. My favourite scene was probably the ominous opening story Himeno was telling Mayu--the horror writing in this game isn't bad, per se, but I do think that scene is at least *one* of the best examples. Considering a lot of the game's advertisable meat is supposed to be this horror writing (ie, the bad ends)...that's not good!  It works in certain RPGMaker games but MAN, the bad end-focused gameplay does NOT feel like it works particularly well here.

Sort of just yakking my jaw, but this game wasted my time pretending that it had something to say, and that always kinda frustrates me. [spoiler]Seriously. That clunky, stupid title drop at the end of -Himeno- is probably the entire reason I'm bothering to write a negative review.[/spoiler] . If you want a sorta mysterious slightly unfamiliar world-feeling game focused on girls with loads of bad ends, just play an RPGMaker game at that point. Play Pocket Mirror.
Achievements are what keep you interested in this game 🤔

Sound of Drop is a messy story with some positives that save it from being atrociously bad.

Mayumi and her friend Himeno visit the mystery-surrounded Manten Aquarium. Then, Mayumi sees her younger sister Mari, who went missing there five years ago, and chases her throughout the aquarium, losing Himeno in the process. Afterwards, a series of strange phenomena occur, and Mayumi has to figure out what's going on, and save Himeno and Mari.

Sound of Drop puts its protagonist Mayumi in a LOT of life-or-death scenarios, and it's up to the reader to correctly pick in the 50/50 to help her survive. Both because the story doesn't do the legwork of getting me to care about Mayumi or any of the other characters and because of the sheer amount of bad endings, these choices, and the resulting bad endings, aren't fun or exciting, they're tedious, and B-movie quality at best. Also, it even sometimes feels like the story is pulled off course just to forcibly insert another opportunity for a bad ending.

Originally, Sound of Drop had only two true endings, but an update four years after its release adds two more and expands the story in other ways. I think without this new material, I would have disliked Sound of Drop even more. The new material focuses on the more interesting characters in the story who were glossed over in favor of Himeno in the original pair of endings. Still, a big issue with both pairs of endings (new & old) is that they don't feel different enough to even justify there being two endings. As I was wrapping up the final ending, I had the feeling that I had just read the same story—maybe presented slightly differently—four different times.

There are a few positives to Sound of Drop. The music and artwork is nice. Again, I like the focus on the side characters in the newer endings. But overall, it's not great. Letterboxd review voice: It's like if they made one of those anomaly, spot-the-difference, friendslop games into a visual novel.

I may have gone through all the routes for this game but I still can't recommend it. I went through everything because I figured I might as well get my money's worth and I like collecting achievements.

Regarding the story, I just...... don't [i]care[/i] about it. When I first started playing, I was having a little fun because the bad ends felt kind of wack (more on endings later) but the game failed to ever make me actually give a ♥♥♥♥ about anyone. I suppose Sayo is my favorite character because she has the most personality and actually has character growth depending on what route you take? Otherwise Mayumi doesn't really change beyond accepting that Mari is actually dead, Himeno doesn't change, Mari doesn't really change [spoiler]except the one route where she realizes she can't have her sister to herself, but that's one route only[/spoiler] but she's dead and a child so I guess she can get a small pass, Kenji doesn't change, Rieko doesn't change, etc.  Hell, the fish change more!  And not only do we hardly have any character growth, but they decided to make the story so insanely complicated (or I'm just too stupid to follow everything) that I think after I'm done writing this I'm going to have to look for a wiki or something to doublecheck some details because I'm confused on a few parts. It felt like they threw in a bunch of plot twists just for the sake of being like "OOooOOoOoOOoo PLOT TWIST!!!!!!!111!!11!"

The game's translation is a bit clunky. It's not like I couldn't understand what was being said, but it wasn't great. That's all I have to say there but I figured I'd mention it considering it IS a VN after all.

Regarding endings, I think the 4 main endings are fine (the NG+ ones are definitely better than the first 2) but jesus christ why are there so many bad ends? And some of them are just TIIIINY variations of each other which feels so stupid and made getting the achievements for getting the bad ends a bit of a chore (I swear to god I'll have that little piano bit from the bad end screen playing in my head for forever).

Anyways. It's not like this game was like pulling teeth but I wouldn't ever come back to it. This is a horror VN but I never felt creeped out by anything or had goosebumps. There was a part that was definitely supposed to be Icky Icky Eek! that I actually just laughed at and that's not me trying to be edgy, I just thought it was so bizarre. Get it on sale I suppose if you're interested?

The thing that scared me the most from this game is how everyone seems to love it.

Sound of Drop is probably one of the most boring vns I've read as of lately and it really surprises me how much people seemed to have enjoyed it. The story has an interesting premise and setting, with some decent enough artwork and an actually surprisingly good ost, but as far as things go that's pretty much all it has to offer.

The story's good parts pretty much end at the premise, as this vn has some of the worst writing I've had to go through if I'm being completely honest. Cutting to the chase here, the vn has absolutely terrible pacing in my opinion, putting a very large focus on info dumps instead of developing characters or actually building tension (which is what you'd normally expect from a horror story). The story doesn't have very long run, being around 5-6 hours long excluding the bad ends, but I'd say around 3-4 hours of that is just the game basically spoon feeding you the entire plot.

The plot isn't really that good either. Avoiding spoilers, the game starts out as what seems to be a more ghost/supernatural centered mystery, but slowly dissolves into a mesh of sci-fi and revenge plot. It's very easy to get lost in all the information the game bombards you with as most of the time they happen during really awkward situations or just totally out of the blue. The characters are generic at most and cardboard at worst, with more than half of them just serving as plot devices. The main villain didn't even feel like a main villain, as you honestly spend more time listening to some random character monologue about the mechanics of the aquarium than time building a relationship with the villain. I didn't even realize I was nearing the end while reading as the entire run of this vn feels like some info dump you'd usually have at the beginning of the story before things start to take off.

Overall this vn just really doesn't give you enough time to build relationships with the cast, or build its own atmosphere, which is a very big no-no when it comes to horror. It focuses too much on trying to make a convoluted plot that it just gets lost in its own story, making for a very unsatisfying game to play through. Things are explained too hastily without much thought, and the actual horror or climax scenes end way too abruptly. This is probably the only vn I've read so far to make me give up on at least trying to 100% it just because of how bored I was reading through it.

3.5/10 wouldn't recommend

I tried really hard to like this game, since I love horror VNs and the core concept is really cool, but it really doesn't work well. I think it's more mediocre than actively bad, but Steam only allows a thumbs up or down. Ultimately, I decided to give it a thumbs down to balance some of the positive reviews, since I ended up pretty underwhelmed. The setting and creepy vibes the game start with get squandered by the end and the plot is kind of all over the place. I got it on sale so I don't regret it and it took me about 4 hours to see everything, but I'm a pretty fast reader, so your mileage may vary.

==More detailed complaints (as spoiler free as possible)==
There are 31 possible ending advertised and 27 of those are BAD ENDs. A bad end fiesta in a horror VN sold me on the game, but in reality, several of the 27 bad ends are repeats that are triggered slightly differently. I think only two of the bad ends actually had a CG attached. So if you were hoping for a bunch of horrifying CGs, this game does not have them (despite the warning at the start of the game). There are maybe 3 "gross" CGs, and one of them is in the trailer, so if you're used to horror, you might be disappointed.

Second, several of the bad ends you get early on make absolutely no sense. There is no logical connection between the decision you made and the ending you get. On more than one occasion you end up in extremely similar situations, but the same option will kill you in one. For example, on two occations you end up cornered and are given the option to "run through" or "not run through." In one of those situations, running through will instantly kill you, but in the other, running through is the only way to survive. The disconnect between logic and death meant at each decision point I just saved, watched the cheap death scene, then reloaded. 

The entire VN has only three branch points: the original game's good and normal routes hinge on a single decision, during new game plus there is a branch point where you move from the original game routes to the plus routes, and then a third branch point where you choose between the plus good and normal routes. That's fine, after all, there are several kinetic VNs I like and they have zero branches, but it's hard to build tension when every decision is either "death" or "continue."

Finally, the plot lacks coherent internal logic. As I mentioned above, the bad endings seem to come out of nowhere, but the game does finally present a why and how you've been dying once you learn the mechanics of the aquarium, which seemed like a pacing problem to me. I was enjoying the New Game+ content a lot more with the knowledge of what the aquarium is, but then discovered there is no objective logic to it. Each route follows a different logic with different antagonists which are incompatible with other routes. That's fine in something with more branches where your decisions are altering things, but since each route is influenced by one minor decision that isn't linked in a logical way to an outcome, it means one comment I made halfway through the game retroactively made a character a psychopath the whole time. One of the Plus routes seemed like it was turning things on its head and genuinely doing something cool, but then the other Plus route contradicted it.

I could talk about how the art and writing are good. I could talk about how the translation is smooth, and how the music and sound direction are on point. I could talk about how the gruesome parts lean into textual descriptions more than in-your-face visual gore, and how I think it uses the reader's imagination to its advantage.

All of these are great points in this game's favour. But Sound of Drop - fall into poison - does one more very important thing. It does what so many otherwise good visual novels fail to do: It contains underage girls and is not horny about any of them. There are no voyeuristic camera angles. There are no compromising positions or tee-hee accidental hand- or eyefuls.  Everyone remains fully dressed. The creep is called out as a creep. Sound of Drop soars over a bar that is lying on the floor while other games in this genre insist on playing limbo with the devil. I know this is an ironic thing to say about a game with so much drowning in it, but it's a breath of fresh air.

Pretty decent horror visual novel. If you don't care about the finer details,[b] the TL;DR is that the game is worth it on sale for sure, 50% off at least. Full price is iffy, not for lack of content but for lack of utilizing its potential. [/b]

[h1] The Goods [/h1]

+ The game has an amazing soundtrack, especially the one at the beginning where an urban legend is being told. It's what made me keep the game and I'm certain that many others felt the same. It's one of those OSTs that you add to your playlist. Definitely the type and quality of music I want to include in my own games if I ever decide to give that a go.

+ The game doesn't overstay its welcome in terms of length. I didn't feel like it was dragging on at any point really. Binge read the whole last ~5 hours or so and hunted all the achievements along the way :D

+ Well executed and interesting twists after certain routes are unlocked, foreshadowed by the info given in certain bad endings. Really changed my perspective on some of the characters.

+ No weird anime things, so I can happily recommend this to other people. I love anime and all but yeah. Being an adult, it's hard to consume it and recommend it to others at times.

+ The bad endings were pretty cool at times, and I really liked the setting of the aquarium. I love marine life :)

+ The price is low enough (especially on sale) that you won't regret buying it. I'm a bit frugal and a very patient person when it comes to games, so it gets my seal of approval on sale (not that that means anything to you all XD).

[h1] The Bads [/h1]

- Lack of voice acting and the game's translation is not the best, so it becomes a bit hard to read at some points. Combined with a lack of CG art for important plot points, it kinda made it hard to take the game seriously at times.

- For a game with so many bad endings, the bad ending cards could come quicker, and locking the controls in the menu until the animation plays out got annoying. You can circumvent this issue by accessing the menu during the bad end cards and just loading from there. But I didn't realize this until I played with a control and accidentally found it out, seeing as the game doesn't have a 'controls' page. I was hoping for a hotkey for saving (not quick saving). Speaking of bad endings...

- Repetitive bad endings. Many of the endings involve the same CG with the main character ending up in water. And sometimes, it feels so lazy. Like, there are no descriptions of the space/environment warping or anything, just a lot of, "And before I know it, I'm underwater."

- Not enough reactions from the main character. I'm not sure if this is a translation issue or a dev issue, but at some points, the story felt like it transitioned way too fast from one scene to another. Something important would happen, and it felt like it had no real impact. The story would just... continue. As mentioned earlier, there is a lack of CGs for certain plot points, so, for example, the main character would be screaming and crying but all we see is a hallway. That issue compounds the feeling that the plot points and happenings seemingly having no impact. 

- The final two routes barely have any choices or bad endings, they mostly become a straight up book. Lots of exposition that gets kind of hard to follow when there is so much of it. I enjoy thinking critically in a VN/any media, but it felt out of place here. Combine that with the rough translations I mentioned earlier, as well as the quick plot transitions, and this easily became the biggest negative for me. 

- It really feels like they didn't use the environment/setting to its full potential. Where are the sharks? Where are the eels? Why isn't there a bad ending where the main character gets eaten by a giant angler fish??? Wasted potential honestly.

[h1] The Verdict [/h1]

= Considering that I am probably more critical of stuff than most, you may enjoy this VN a good chunk more than me. I'd check it out (again, especially on sale) if any of the positives interested you. The negatives don't feel like they stem from utter laziness or a noticeable lack of effort.

= Overall, I give the novel a ~6.5/10, where a 5/10 is just okay/passing. Despite the lengthy negatives I wrote about, the novel was <$4 and I did genuinely enjoy my time reading it, so I definitely recommend giving it a go. I feel like one can be critical of something but still enjoy the ride :)

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[b]1.[/b]
Manten Aquarium, a place for fun and amazement at the numerous exhibits of sealife surrounding it. There are some rumors that the place is haunted, where the water turns into blood and there are fishes with human faces lurking about. Are they true though? That is what best friend duo Mayumi Nakanobe and Himeno Tamagawa want to seek. Mayumi has a link to Manten Aquarium, she lost her little sister Mari several years ago during a family trip.
	At the aquarium with Himeno, Mayumi spots glimpses and hears her long lost sister, Mari. Straying away from Himeno to investigate, Mayumi wanders further into Manten Aquarium but later on finds out that there is something more to the place, something sinister beneath its depths. Now that those urban legends are true and Red Manten Aquarium is real, Mayumi needs to regroup and find out the truth behind the ethereal waters.
	Overall, the concept is definitely interesting and this visual novel handles it fine for the most part, there are some things that do get in the way which I will talk about down in the Cons below.
[b]2.[/b]
The characters are decent with Mayumi being a bit sheepish compared to the energetic Himeno, Sayo Sakuragi being stoic and blunt, Miku Minato being the opposite of Sayo, and Mari genuinely wanting to take care of Mayumi. They have to go through the horrors of Red Manten Aquarium with a brave face and all have their moments, like [spoiler] Orcas swimming around Sayo, Mayumi witnessing the floating heads in the tanks, or Himeno wanting to help Mayumi even if she is on the brink of collapsing. [/spoiler]
[b]3.[/b] 
The art is lovely to look at with vibrant backgrounds that are absolutely important if you're going for an aquatic setting. There is also the character art by [url=https://twitter.com/shiokojii]塩こうじ (Shio Koji)[/url] that is great. The CG art is also excellent by showing the disturbing events but also help enhance the characters actions and feelings like when Mayumi was surrounded by Jellyfish.
[b]4.[/b]
The soundtrack is fantastic like the title track "Sound of Drop" with its piano and light choir gives off the despair when Mayumi lost Mari, but then when the little chimes similar to a music box show up, it's like a somber reunion. Several of the tracks are suited for its horror scenes but there are also some lighthearted tracks such as "Midafternoon" that feels like you're just taking a walk through a shopping district or in this case, the aquarium. "Kanashii Koto (悲しいこと)" is a great one too as it is where a pivotal moment comes near the end and the track just fits it so well. Let's not forget about the Opening theme "Shizuku no Oto" an absolute banger too, [url=https://www.shotamatsumoto.net/]Shota Matsumoto[/url] and [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/kuyuri9/featured]Kuyuri[/url] did a great job on the track.
[b]5.[/b]
The use of an ending tracker is an extremely helpful feature.




[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[b]1.[/b]
The story concept is good as I said, but how it handles it around the third act does get a bit muddy. It goes heavily into a tell don't show scenario on whichever route you chose. It's either one antagonist explaining everything to you or a different character explaining everything to you. It also leads me to a character issue.
[b]2.[/b]
The characters, mainly the main protagonists and Reiko, I think they were fine, maybe a bit flat background wise. Now the issues come with [spoiler]Hiyoshi[/spoiler]. I think they wanted this character to have a real role in the story but I think pushing him to be something greater felt like a mistake. Despite having several scenes dedicated to him, I think he should have stayed a neutral entity. He was a side character, nothing more or less. [spoiler] Hiyoshi having a role in Reiko's plan and a bloody childhood[/spoiler] felt suddenly added in, especially since this is the true ending. Having that being explained, just felt strange.

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
The story is interesting but it drops a bit later on with a heavy "tell don't show" portion along with Hiyoshi being made a character with a larger role but it just misses the target with him.

[h1]すぐ分かる概要[/h1]
[list]
[*]正直、どちらかと言えばおすすめ、程度。
[*]無駄な導入が少なく、ホラー要素までのテンポが良い。
[*]水族館の雰囲気が十分に伝わってくる。
[/list]


[h3]感想[/h3]

[b][u]おすすめする理由[/u][/b]

　私は「どちらかと言えば」おすすめという印象でした。
　決してつまらなかったわけではないのですが、どういうわけか読了感が全く存在せず、今でも不思議な感覚です。

　エンディングの総数が31個という、やる気をそがれる量ですが、原則的に一本道なので、その点は心配ありませんでした。
　これで好感度のような仕組みが働いていたら、評価を翻していたと思います。（一部の実績には関係しますけれど。）

　ビジュアルノベルなので、理不尽に追い掛け回されることもないですし、ホラーが苦手な方でも手を出しやすいように思います。
　結論として「水族館」と「ホラー」の2つが刺さる方ならば、購入して損は無いでしょう。


[b][u]ゲームの特徴[/u][/b]

　水族館や展示された生き物への想いを、随所から感じる作品です。

　メニューを開くと現在地に応じて、さながら水族館にいるかのようなガイダンスまで表示されます。特筆すべきは背景と物語の兼ね合いです。本当に水族館を歩いている気分に浸れます。

　クオリティの高い、オープニングやエンディングの楽曲も魅力的です。ボイス無しのゲームであることが作用し、演出が引き立っているように思えました。

　加えて、UIもシンプルで素晴らしいのですが・・・汚点は『クイックセーブ』にあります。

　本作は通常のセーブスロットが100個存在し、クイックセーブで使われるのは、不可視で別枠の1つです。ここまでなら普通なのですが、読み込むための『クイックロード』は「最新のセーブデータ」が対象になっているようでした。

　つまり、通常のセーブを行ってしまうと、クイックセーブのデータは恒久的に読み込めなくなります。そのため、選択肢が表示される毎に自動でクイックセーブがされる親切設計も、敢えて作品に掛けて言うならば『水の泡』です。

　プレーされる際は手動セーブを駆使しましょう。


[b][u]気が付いたこと等[/u][/b]

　地の文を筆頭に、文章が読みやすかったです。そのため、不規則に振られているルビが邪魔で仕方がありませんでした。
　固有名詞はともかく、同じ言葉でもルビが有ったり無かったりと、一貫性の無さに集中力を削がれました。

　特筆すべき難しい言葉は使われていないので、初めから一切無しでもよかったのではないでしょうか。
　その上、後半ほどルビが減るので、書いている側が面倒になって来たのではないかと、メタな方向に思考を持っていかれました。中でも [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2807245220]設定ミス[/url][/b] を見かけたときには、没入感が消滅しましたね。

　そして、全体の読みやすさが災いして、一部の [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2807149417]日本語の誤用[/url][/b] が相対的に目立ってしまっていました。繰り返しますが、全体的に文章が素晴らしいことは確かです。


[h3]余談[/h3]

[b][u]ガイド[/u][/b]

　私がプレーした段階で、日本語での攻略ガイドが存在しなかったため、作成してみました。

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2808502720

It's a good story, the translation is a bit weird, though. It feels like a machine translator or someone using a dictionary translated it. It's a unique enough story for me to ignore that, but I'd advise people to get it on sale.
